mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen for three consecutive weeks (-38.6 to -29.6), and this commuting recovery pulls discretionary foot traffic back into retail corridors, so the four-week mean of RETAIL_REC rises relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is at or below its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to rise for at least two further weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT converts into retail spending only when RESIDENTIAL simultaneously falls, because the joint movement identifies genuine out-of-home substitution rather than transit-only commuting; this interaction produces a higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week in the same week that RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: Weeks in which TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls jointly are followed by RETAIL_REC declines as often as by increases.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed from -17.7 to -9.9; once it crosses -10 the household provisioning routine is normalized enough that discretionary shopping re-attaches to the same errands, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -10 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: Weeks where GROCERY_PHARM prints above -10 are followed by a RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days that is not higher than the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen four weeks running (12.4 to 10.6), indicating decay in stay-at-home compliance; each further point of residential decline releases discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days while RESIDENTIAL continues its week-on-week decline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovery has stalled (-58.4 to -59.1) while TRANSIT keeps improving (-32.7 to -29.6), indicating a seasonal rotation of outdoor leisure demand toward indoor commercial venues; this substitution raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean fails to improve for two consecutive weeks while TRANSIT rises in both
failure_condition: Periods where PARKS stalls and TRANSIT rises are followed by flat or lower RETAIL_REC over four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Inside a phased-reopening regime, joint weekly improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects the lifting of mobility restrictions, and retail capacity follows with a one-week lag, so RETAIL_REC is higher one week ahead.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week while TRANSIT also rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -36.9 to -30.4 in the final week
regime_hint: phased reopening with capacity limits being lifted
failure_condition: Within a phased-reopening regime, a joint WORKPLACES-and-TRANSIT weekly rise is followed by a next-week RETAIL_REC that is flat or lower.

mechanism_narrative: Fast GROCERY_PHARM recovery absorbs the limited out-of-home trip budget of households, draining discretionary visits, so RETAIL_REC stays below its recent level over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 points week-on-week in two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After two consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM gains above 2 points, the next-14-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal cooling keeps park-based leisure suppressed (PARKS pinned near -59) and the +4.1 point weekly jump in RETAIL_REC is a persistence signal, so RETAIL_REC one week ahead is higher than the current week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -41.7 to -37.6 in the final week
failure_condition: One week after a weekly RETAIL_REC jump of +3 points or more, RETAIL_REC is lower than in the jump week.
